pitch.topic: A night babysitting job. The baby monitor shows a tall figure bent over the crib, but the parents are watching their live camera app from dinner and swear the nursery is empty.
pitch.logline: You're babysitting alone and the baby monitor shows something tall bent over the crib. The parents, watching their live camera app from a restaurant, swear the nursery is empty. Both of you are telling the truth, and that's the scary part.

pitch.twist: The baby monitor runs exactly ten minutes behind. Nobody was lying. The parents' app is live, and by the time Mrs. Hale looked, the shape was already hiding behind the nursery door, out of the camera's view. Everything you watched had already happened. It stood behind the door while you waved, slipped out after you (the hallway motion at eleven fifty-one), and has been standing behind you in the guest room ever since. The "Shhh." was real, not the muted monitor. Final sting: the parents' live feed finally shows it at your shoulder. It whispers "Shhh. You'll wake her." and climbs back to the nursery, and your monitor won't show you what it does up there for ten more minutes.
pitch.plants:
1) The fridge note, read aloud in Part 1: "Monitor's old. Runs a little behind!" It sounds like a joke about a slow, cheap device.
2) Every monitor_screen stamp is exactly ten minutes behind the top-left clock (11:30 at 11:40, 11:34 at 11:44, 11:36 at 11:46, 11:41 at 11:51, 11:48 at 11:58). It is visible in every shot and never mentioned until Part 3.
3) Mrs. Hale's four-camera screenshot (Part 1) and her photo of you (Part 2) carry stamps that match the top-left clock (11:42, 11:48). Her app is live; your monitor isn't.
4) Part 1's last beat: "Now your monitor looks just like her screenshot." Your monitor literally catches up to what she saw earlier, with a one-frame overlay.
5) The shape hides behind the nursery door (Part 1). In Part 2: "You don't look behind the door.", you leave the door open a crack, and two dim red dots sit in the door gap for a few frames.
6) You wave at the camera twice and Mrs. Hale sends the 11:48 photo (Part 2). That exact image plays on the monitor at 11:58 in Part 3.
7) Mr. Hale's alert: hallway motion at eleven fifty-one, when you've been downstairs since eleven fifty (Part 2).
8) "The sound is muted." (Part 1), the crossed-out speaker icon in every monitor shot, then the "Shhh." you blame on the monitor, with a 10%-opacity silhouette behind you (Part 2).
9) The GUEST RM feed in Part 1's screenshot shows the parents can see your room, which sets up the final live screenshot.
10) The shape's finger-to-face gesture (Part 1) marks it as the one who shushes, paying off in "Shhh." and "Shhh. You'll wake her."
pitch.why_it_works: It's clearly different from the used premises: no future-self messages, no rules, no bathtub, no voice-mimic knocking, no doubles or codewords. The horror runs on a simple, believable device, a laggy baby monitor, and the "parents say it can't be there" setup is honest on both sides. That makes the reveal feel earned instead of cheated. The twist can be solved on screen: sharp viewers can compare the top-left clock with the monitor stamp in every shot, which drives rewatches and "look at the timestamps!" comments. There's dramatic irony throughout (the door you never check, the motion alert, the muted whisper), so viewers dread things the narrator is talking themself out of. Each part opens on the strangest image (a figure over the crib, something hiding, someone walking in) inside three seconds, and something new happens every 8-10 s. The ending turns the twist into a ticking clock: the parents finally see it, it heads back to the nursery, and you're ten minutes behind. That makes the closing question ("What would you do with ten minutes?") easy and fun to answer. Production: almost everything is screens, a note, a hallway and silhouettes, so it suits the 2D stick-figure style, and it only needs two new scene types (monitor_screen, cctv_grid). It's TikTok-safe: no gore, no swearing, and the baby is never harmed on screen; the threat is only implied.

SERIES RULES FOR THIS SCENE: (a) ONE nursery camera only, a small dome high in the ceiling corner. (b) FIXED NURSERY LAYOUT, drawn once and reused: crib center-right holding a tiny white swaddled bundle (Wren); a tall slatted CLOSET door on the left wall, fully CLOSED; a small red nightlight near the floor; the nursery door on the far right. (e) The monitor is muted all series: monitor beats never play static or nursery sounds, only off-screen score or room tone, and any noise inside the nursery is drawn as a small silent red sfx word on the feed. final.changes: I applied every review note. All of them held up, and where two notes described the same problem, I merged them into one fix. COUNTS AND TIMING: Each part is 168 words, split on spaces. If hyphenated numbers count as two words, the totals are 168, 171 and 169, still inside 165-195. I re-timed every beat from one TTS budget: 2.5 words per second, 0.3 s per full stop, and short holds for visual moments. No beat is crammed any more. For example, 'Toward the camera. Two red eyes.' now has 3 s, the Part 2 recap has 5 s and 'Shhh. You'll wake her.' has 3 s. The parts run 84 s, 84 s and 83 s. The suggested slower budget (2 words per second plus 0.4 s per stop) cannot fit 165 words into 85 s, so treat these windows as estimates and reset them from the real TTS audio. Every quote is a verbatim substring of its narration, and the narration contains no digits. BLOCKER, MUTED MONITOR: No monitor_screen beat plays static or nursery sound any more. They use only off-screen score or room tone. Door and closet sounds are drawn on the feed as silent red words ('sssllide', 'creak'). The spoken 'muted all night' beat is cut. The MUTED icon now pays off visually: it pulses in sharp focus right after the whisper. CLIFFHANGER AND PREMISE DISTANCE: Part 2 now ends at 12:00 with stamp 11:50. The closet slides open and the thing unfolds ('Where is it going?' / 'Where did it go?'), so there is no 'you walk in' mystery double. In Part 3, past-you appears only once, as a narrator rewind labeled 'That's you, ten minutes ago.' The Part 3 recap hook is rewritten to match and puts the strange part first: 'Something tall unfolded from the nursery closet.' I avoided 'out of the closet' and 'steps out' near 'closet' because of the slang double meaning. STORY LOGIC: (1) Your text is now honest: 'I'm in the nursery. The closet is open.' Mrs. Hale waves it off ('It never shuts right. There you are! Wave.'), and the narration makes the fear explicit: 'You don't open the closet. You can't.' (2) Mrs. Hale is normal now. Her replies have typing dots, 'She checks her app.' replaces 'instantly', 'I'll watch you on the app' is softened to 'I'll watch on the app', and the dinner became a wedding ('Cute! Last dance!' at 11:49, with a reception murmur). (3) The Mr. Hale thread now closes. His text reads 'Hallway cam caught you at eleven fifty. Then motion at eleven fifty-one. Too dark to see.' You answer 'That wasn't me.', he answers 'Getting Dana.', and Part 3's stacked lock screen shows 'Getting Dana.' above 'Mrs. Hale sent a photo'. 'And now, nobody's watching' became 'She puts her phone away.' (4) The black 11:51 HALL thumbnail now has two faint red pinpoints far above head height, and Part 3 rings them. (5) The replay of the wave now shows the same red dots as Part 2, held for a full second and ringed. (6) The 10% silhouette sliver stays at screen-right behind your head in the 12:00 close-up. Part 3 has no guest-room wide shot before 12:01. (7) You now shut your eyes at 11:54 and open them at midnight, which explains why you never saw yourself on the delayed monitor. (8) The fridge-note correction is now a narrator overlay: a ruler-straight red strike-through plus a typed '-10 MIN' stamp, merged with the clock-versus-stamp rings. It is no longer new handwriting in the house. STAGING: There is ONE ceiling-corner nursery camera, and the old monitor is a second receiver of it. Mrs. Hale's live views are always drawn as her app (a phone frame with the bun avatar and 'Hale Cams • LIVE'), never as the chunky monitor. The monitor stamp sits directly under the top-left clock, the muted icon sits under the REC dot, and nothing important goes in the lower third or the right-hand button column. phone_chat beats show only your thumb. The GUEST RM camera is at the frame's top-right, and its tile is a high front three-quarter view. The hoodie is now a hood rim around the whole head. The shape always stands behind your LEFT shoulder, which is screen-right, matching the right-panned whisper, and in the from-behind shot it passes you on screen-left. It is now about one and a half times your height and ducks through doors. The head turn is now a visible lift and tilt on a bending neck, with unlit sockets that light later. In the end sting the eyes light first, then the head tilts. The one-frame overlay is now a 1.5 s A/B flicker. Part 3's climb ends as the shape fades into the corridor and is carried by sound only, and Part 2's CREAK words sit on the corridor floor ahead of you. RETENTION AND SAFETY: The Part 2 recap is cut to 12 words ('It hid in the nursery closet, and only your monitor saw it.'). Part 3 cuts the muted beat and the 'Look closer' beat and merges the clocks with the fridge note, so the live GUEST RM reveal lands at 0:43 instead of 0:52. The final comment question is now 'When did you first notice the monitor's clock? Comment the time.', which drives rewatches and no longer asks about letting harm reach the baby. Wren is never touched. Only monitor_screen and cctv_grid are new scene types; rule_card is an existing type.

issues.problem: The script says the monitor is muted, but its sound design keeps playing sounds from the nursery. Part 1 beats 1, 4 and 5 run a static hiss and a swelling static right under the line "The sound is muted." Part 2 beat 18 (the cliffhanger) plays "a slow, distorted door creak through the static." Part 3 beats 1, 2 and 9 add a door creak, a door bump against the wall, a wooden slide and a stretching creak, all "through the static." Part 3 beat 11 then pays off with "The monitor was muted all night" to prove the whisper was real. Viewers have just heard a door creak come out of that monitor, so this payoff feels like a cheat and the plant is contradicted by the audio.
issues.fix: Make every monitor_screen beat silent as far as the monitor goes. Use only off-screen score (drone, heartbeat, ringing) or plain room tone, with no static hiss and no nursery sounds. Show the door creak, door bump and wooden slide as silent red sfx words drawn on the feed. A door swinging open in total silence is also creepier and sells MUTED.

issues.problem: Your text "I'm in the nursery. It's empty." contradicts what you already know. At the end of Part 1 you watched it fold itself into the closet ("But nothing ever left that room."). Part 2's own recap says it "just hid in a closet," and one beat earlier you stare at the closet gap. Calling the room empty, not mentioning the closet to Mrs. Hale, and leaving Wren alone with it all have no reason behind them. Viewers will read it as a plot hole, not as suspense.
issues.fix: Give a reason on screen and keep the text honest. Example: change your text to "I'm in the nursery. The closet is open." and her reply to "It never shuts right. There you are! Wave." Or keep the text but add a narrated excuse that uses the misdirect: "Her camera is live. Your old monitor is wrong. It has to be."

issues.problem: Mrs. Hale's live app is drawn with the same monitor_screen scene as your baby monitor: the same nursery drawing, the same ceiling angle, only less grain and a small LIVE tag. This happens in beat 4 (door push at 11:48) and beat 9 (the wave at 11:49). Nothing in the narration or on screen says whose screen this is. A one-time viewer will likely think your baby monitor showed you walking in live at 11:48. That contradicts Part 3's 'the picture is ten minutes late' and muddies the cliffhanger at 11:58, which reuses the same framing.
issues.fix: Draw both beats inside a phone frame with Mrs. Hale's app header (bun avatar, 'Hale Cams • LIVE'). Or show them as one enlarged tile of the cctv_grid style already set up as 'her app' in Part 1. Keep the chunky old-monitor frame only for your delayed monitor.

issues.problem: The replay of the wave (grainy, stamp 11:49) says "The closet gap stays black at the left edge." Part 2 beat 9 shows the same wave live and has two dim red dots glow in the closet gap as the arm drops. Two cameras showing the same moment now disagree, which breaks the rewatch clue the script calls a deliberate plant.
issues.fix: In Part 3 beat 4, show the same red dots in the gap as the arm drops, and hold them longer than four frames this time. Have a red ring snap around them so the Part 2 Easter egg pays off on screen.

issues.problem: The Mr. Hale thread is left hanging and doesn't add up. At 11:53 he reports unexplained motion in the hallway outside his baby's room, you answer "No.", his typing dots appear and then vanish, and nobody reacts for eight minutes. Part 3 never explains the vanished dots, so viewers may think something happened to him. Part 3 beat 12 then says "Mrs. Hale is finally watching" with nothing shown that made her look. It also contradicts Part 2 beat 10's "And now, nobody's watching," because Mr. Hale is checking the cameras four beats later.
issues.fix: Replace the vanishing dots with a short reply, for example "Getting Dana." Then Part 3 beat 12's notification is the payoff of that line (for example, a stacked lock screen showing Mr. Hale: "Getting Dana." above "Mrs. Hale sent a photo"). Change Part 2 beat 10's line to "Nobody's watching the cameras now," or drop that half of the line.

issues.problem: The proof that the hallway motion 'wasn't you' is too thin. The on-screen clock puts you in the upstairs hallway at 11:50 (beat 11). Part 3 beat 9 shows the shape leaving right behind you at stamp 11:50. The hallway camera must also have caught you at 11:47 and 11:50, yet Mr. Hale asks only about 11:51. In a story whose whole puzzle is clocks being off, a one-minute gap invites 'that was just you.'
issues.fix: In the black HALL thumbnail, draw two faint red pinpoints near the top of the frame, far above a person's head. 'Too dark to see.' stays true for him, and it becomes a visible plant. Ring the pinpoints in Part 3 beat 10. Optionally, move the ping to eleven fifty-two and let the shape wait just inside the nursery door (matching the Part 2 shadows) before it glides out in Part 3 beat 9.

issues.problem: The 11:58 face close-up says "The darkness behind your head looks empty." Per Part 2 beat 17 and the series notes, the shape has stood behind your RIGHT shoulder since 11:54, and Part 3 beat 13 reveals it at 'the exact spot of the faint silhouette in Part 2.' Rewatchers checking that spot at 11:58 will find it missing.
issues.fix: Keep the 10%-opacity silhouette (a sliver of its long arm or the raised finger) at the right edge behind your head in this close-up. Do the same in any later guest-room wide shot before 12:01, such as Part 3 beat 5.

issues.problem: A red marker crosses out the fridge note and adds '10 MINUTES LATE' 'in jagged red handwriting that is clearly not hers.' This reads as someone, presumably the shape, physically writing on the note in the kitchen. Nothing in the story allows that: you are frozen in the guest room and the shape is behind you. A one-time viewer will ask who wrote it, and the script never answers.
issues.fix: Make it clearly a narrator graphic, not something that happens in the house. Use a red stamp or caption laid over the note in the same typeface as '-10 MIN', or cut to a rule_card reading TEN MINUTES LATE. Don't make it a new line in someone else's handwriting.

issues.problem: Part 2's cliffhanger shows a figure walking into the nursery upstairs, with your white hand and your glowing phone, while you sit downstairs. Part 3 then opens on "It's you." That is the same "two of you in two places" picture as banned premise 2 (one mom at the door, one in the hallway), and it sits right next to premise 1 (you, shifted in time). The user asked for a story that is "not completely the same". This is the biggest cliffhanger in the series, so it is where the series is most likely to read as a reskin.
issues.fix: End Part 2 at 12:00 (stamp 11:50) on the monitor instead. The closet slides open, the thing unfolds and glides out the nursery door: "On the monitor, the closet slides open. It steps out. Where is it going?" (The viewer already heard the whisper at 11:54, which makes this a fair clue.) In Part 3, show past-you on the monitor only as quick proof of the delay ("That's you. Ten minutes ago."), never as a mystery "someone". Rewrite the Part 3 recap hook to match.

issues.problem: In Part 1 you watched the thing fold itself into the nursery closet. In Part 2 you stand in front of that same closet, see it open a crack, and text "I'm in the nursery. It's empty." You also never tell the Hales about the closet. Viewers will read this as the main character lying or being dumb, not as scared, and it weakens the fair-twist logic.
issues.fix: Have her text something true that she sends out of fear: "I'm in the nursery. Wren's fine." Then make the avoidance explicit in the next beat: "You don't open the closet. You can't."

issues.problem: The alibi is too thin. You walked down that same hallway at about 11:50. Mr. Hale's ping is 11:51, and the clock only shows whole minutes. "You've been down here since eleven fifty" proves almost nothing, so your flat "No." sounds wrong, and viewers will comment "that was literally you." The hall cam should also have caught you at 11:47 and 11:50, yet he only asks about 11:51.
issues.fix: Make the ping clearly not you. Mr. Hale: "Hallway cam caught you at eleven fifty. Then motion again at eleven fifty-one. Too dark to see." You: "That wasn't me." Part 3's echo of "Too dark to see." still works.

issues.problem: "She answers instantly" has no typing dots and a shaking bubble. Together with "I'm watching the nursery camera right now" and later "I'll watch you on the app", it marks Mrs. Hale as sinister or fake. Part 3 never pays this off, because she turns out to be a normal mom. A "fake parent is texting you" reading also puts the story right next to banned premise 2.
issues.fix: Drop "instantly" and the no-dots shake. Give her normal typing dots and narrate "She checks her app." Or, if the instant reply stays, pay it off in Part 3 with a real reason she already had the app open.

issues.problem: The recap hook is 18 words in one breath. At a slow TTS pace, "hid in a closet" lands at about 4-5 s and "empty" at about 7 s, which breaks the 3-second rule. "Something on the baby monitor" can also be heard as something sitting on top of the device. "The parents swear" is wrong too: only Mrs. Hale said it.
issues.fix: Cut it to about 12 words with the strange part first, for example: "It hid in the nursery closet, and only your monitor saw it."

issues.problem: "Someone is walking into the nursery on the baby monitor, and you're alone downstairs." The part that makes this strange ("you're alone") comes last, at about 5-6 s at a slow pace, so the first 3 seconds are just setup.
issues.fix: Front-load it: "You're home alone, and someone just walked into the nursery." Adjust this if the Part 2 cliffhanger changes.

issues.problem: "Wait ten minutes and watch" asks viewers whether they would let something reach a sleeping baby while they watch it on delay, and it is the last thing said before the sting. It reads as callous, invites comments imagining harm to the baby, and puts "baby in danger" front and center for moderation. That can limit how far the video reaches on the For You page.
issues.fix: Keep the engagement tied to the twist but safe, for example "When did you notice the monitor's clock? Comment the time." This also drives rewatches of Parts 1-2. Or use "Would you run upstairs, or call the Hales first? Comment below."

issues.problem: "The Hales are at dinner" at 11:40 PM, then "Cute! Food's here." at 11:49 PM, even though they left before eight. To American viewers, food arriving near midnight sounds off, and commenters will nitpick it.
issues.fix: "The Hales are at a wedding." plus "Cute! First dance!", with a reception murmur instead of restaurant noise. Or "The Hales are at a late show." plus "Cute! Show's starting."

issues.problem: The main clue for the twist, the monitor time stamp, sits bottom-left, and the crossed-out speaker icon sits bottom-right. On TikTok those areas are covered by the username, caption and sound ticker (left) and the like/comment/share column (right), and the big word-by-word captions also sit low. Most viewers will never see the ten-minute gap, so the twist won't feel fair.
issues.fix: Put the stamp in the upper third of the monitor image, level with the top-left clock so the two can be compared at a glance. Move the muted icon up into the central safe zone. Apply this to every monitor_screen in all three parts.

issues.problem: Several beat windows are too short for a slow, ominous voice. They will push the word-timed visual cues (eyes lighting on "Two red eyes", red rings snapping on words) out of sync. Examples: P1 0:53-0:55, "Toward the camera. Two red eyes." (6 words and two full stops in 2 s); P1 1:10-1:15 (14 words and two voices in 5 s, about 170 wpm); P2 0:00-0:07 (18 words); P3 0:00-0:05 and 0:26-0:31 (14 words each in 5 s); P3 1:03-1:05, a "very low, slow" whisper of "Shhh. You'll wake her." in 2 s. The script averages about 138 wpm, but these beats would need 150-180 wpm.
issues.fix: Generate the TTS first and set the beat windows from the real audio lengths. As a rough budget, allow about 2 words per second plus about 0.4 s per full stop. Otherwise trim those lines. Check that each part still lands between 65 and 85 s.

issues.problem: "10 MINUTES LATE" appears in "jagged red handwriting that is clearly not hers". That says something in the house wrote on the fridge note, an ability the story never sets up or explains, so viewers will ask "who wrote that?" It also reuses the "new line in different handwriting" device, which belongs to the earlier rules-note style series.
issues.fix: Show it as an obvious graphic overlay instead: a red strike-through plus a red typed label such as "-10 MIN", not handwriting inside the story world.

issues.problem: From about 0:11 to 0:49 the payoff part mostly re-explains: the wave, two clocks, the fridge note, the side-by-side, the screenshot, the unfolding, the hallway ping and the muted icon. Only the unfolding beat is new footage. "And that whisper? The monitor was muted all night." repeats something Part 2 already settled with the MUTED pulse. That is a long stretch without anything new, which hurts retention on TikTok.
issues.fix: Cut the muted beat, cut either the "Look closer" CCTV beat or the side-by-side, and merge the clock comparison with the fridge note. That brings the live GUEST RM reveal about 8 s sooner.

issues.problem: Impossible camera geometry. The messenger UI fills the frame head-on, which puts the camera where your eyes are, yet 'Your face, lit red from below, sits at the bottom edge of the frame'. One viewpoint cannot see both the front of the screen and the front of your face. Part 2 beat 6 does the same ('Your face glows at the bottom edge').
issues.fix: In both phone_chat beats, show only your thumb at the bottom edge, in a red glow. If the face matters, cut to a separate 1 s face_closeup instead of compositing it under the UI.

issues.problem: The GUEST RM camera is placed inconsistently. Bedroom shots (P1 b2, P2 b12/b17, P3 b15) draw it 'in the top corner of the room', visible in a front-facing shot. That puts it on the back wall behind you, so it would film your back. Yet the tile here and in P3 b13 shows 'phone glow on your face'. 'Hood outline visible' is a back-of-head detail ('hood outline on the back of the head'), so a front view contradicts it too. The animator cannot draw the climax reveal (P3 b13, 'eyes aimed straight at the lens') consistently.
issues.fix: Put the camera high on the NEAR end of a side wall, at the frame's top-RIGHT edge (top-left holds the series clock), angled back at you. Its tile is then a high front three-quarter view that matches the bedroom shots. Redefine the hoodie as a hood rim drawn around the whole head, so it reads from the front (P1 b12, P2 b8, P3 b3, P3 b13).

issues.problem: Left/right mirror conflict. Every bedroom and GUEST RM shot is front-facing, so a shape 'behind your RIGHT shoulder' (P2 b17, P3 b13, P3 b15) appears on SCREEN-LEFT. But 'SHHH.' breathes in 'from the right edge of the frame', and the whisper and breath are 'panned hard right' (P2 b16, P3 b15, P3 b16). The viewer hears and reads it on the right, then sees it on the left.
issues.fix: Lock one screen side. Change every scene_detail 'behind your RIGHT shoulder' to 'behind your LEFT shoulder (screen-right in front-facing shots)'. The narration never says left or right, so no word changes. In P3 b17's from-behind shot, have it pass you on screen-left.

issues.problem: The twist's key clues sit in TikTok's UI overlay zones. The monitor stamp is bottom-left, under the caption and username text. The crossed-out speaker / MUTED icon is bottom-right, under the like/comment/share column. The big word-by-word captions also compete for the lower third. The fair-play stamp and the 'muted all night' plant can be hidden on a real phone.
issues.fix: For every monitor_screen beat, move the stamp into the upper safe area, on the monitor bezel just below the top-left series clock. Move the muted icon to upper-right under the REC dot. Keep captions in the vertical center band.

issues.problem: The head turn cannot be read. The head is a blank round silhouette with no mouth and its eyes are unlit until 0:53, so a 'round head [that] starts to rotate slowly toward the lens' looks identical at every frame. The narration 'Its head turns. Slowly.' has nothing visible to show. The Part 3 end card (b21, 'turns its head toward the viewer' before the eyes light) has the same problem.
issues.fix: Make the turn a silhouette change. The head lifts from hanging over the crib and tilts up on a visible bending neck line toward the lens. Two faint dark-grey (unlit) eye sockets slide into view as it turns, then light red in b14. In P3 b21, light the eyes first and then tilt the head.

issues.problem: 'For one frame, Mrs. Hale's 11:42 NURSERY tile is laid over the monitor image'. One frame (~33-42 ms) cannot be perceived, so the viewer never sees the match that the narration claims ('matches her screenshot. Exactly.').
issues.fix: Hold a 1-1.5 s A/B flicker between the two images (3-4 alternations), or a brief side-by-side, then drop back to the '11:36 PM' push-in on the gap.

issues.problem: Camera identity is undefined. The fridge note separates the 'Old monitor' from the 'Cameras on my phone', which implies two nursery cameras. Two cameras cannot share one viewpoint, but the script needs the grainy monitor and her clean feed to match 'line for line' (P1 b17, P2 b4 note, P3 b7). An animator drawing two devices will give them different angles and break the proof.
issues.fix: State in P1 b1 scene_detail that there is only ONE nursery camera, in the ceiling corner, and the old monitor is a second (delayed) receiver of it. Draw one camera and identical framing in every nursery view.

issues.problem: Continuity between the same moment on the same camera. In P2 b9, two red dots glow in the closet gap 'as the arm drops' during the wave. The P3 replay of that exact moment says 'The closet gap stays black at the left edge.' Rewatchers who compare the two will see a contradiction.
issues.fix: Add the same ~4-frame dim red dots in the closet gap as past-you's arm drops in P3 b4, with the same timing as P2 b9 (or remove them from both).

issues.problem: The shape's scale cannot be drawn consistently. It is defined as 'nearly twice your height' (~3.2 m for a teen), but here it 'unfolds to full height: its head almost touches the ceiling' (~1.5x) and then 'glides out of the door' (a door is ~1.25x your height). In P3 b17 it 'ducks through the doorway'. The animator has no single scale for the rooms.
issues.fix: Redefine the look as 'about one and a half times your height, head brushing the ceiling'. Change 'glides out of the door' to 'ducks low and glides out of the door'.

issues.problem: Stairs are not part of the hallway asset, and the beat is overloaded. In 4 s the shape must duck through the guest-room door, walk the corridor, reach the stairs and start climbing, at a 'slow' pace. P2 b2 also draws stairs inside 'hallway', and puts 'CREAK' 'beside your feet' in a back-of-head framing where your feet are out of frame.
issues.fix: P3 b17: end the shot as it fades into the black corridor, and let the 'step... step...' sfx and one stair creak carry the climb. P2 b2: place the CREAK words on the corridor floor ahead of you. Alternatively, add stairwell as an allowed third new scene type for both beats.
